l4_steps.name: Verify ETOPS route approval in OpSpecs
l4_steps.input: Planned route, aircraft registration, OpSpec C057 reference
l4_steps.output: ETOPS route authorization confirmed; approved diversion time threshold recorded
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ETOPS-routed flights pre-validated against OpSpecs before release
l4_steps.pain_point: OpSpec revisions under FAR 121.161 / ICAO Doc 10085 require 30-day authority lead time; last-minute network re-routing post-approval is operationally prohibited and forces costly re-planning

l4_steps.name: Confirm aircraft ETOPS certification level
l4_steps.input: Aircraft registration, current maintenance release status
l4_steps.output: ETOPS certification level confirmed (e.g. 120 / 180 / 240 min) and recorded against flight
l4_steps.kpi: Zero ETOPS departures without valid airworthiness certificate and ETOPS approval on record
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS certification can be suspended mid-rotation due to maintenance findings; AMOS aircraft status must be queried in real time — stale cache data in dispatch systems has caused near-misses on ETOPS eligibility checks

l4_steps.name: Retrieve ETOPS alternate airport weather forecasts
l4_steps.input: Planned ETOPS alternate list, estimated departure time, flight duration
l4_steps.output: TAF and METAR reports for all alternates within ETOPS diversion circle
l4_steps.kpi: Weather data currency ≤1 hour before departure; TAF coverage ≥18 hours ahead of ETP crossing
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote oceanic alternates (e.g., NFFN Nadi, PGUM Guam, BIKF Keflavik) have sparse observation networks; TAF accuracy degrades beyond 12 hours, leaving critical ETP windows with low-confidence forecasts

l4_steps.name: Validate ETOPS alternate airport operational status
l4_steps.input: Alternate airport list, current NOTAM bulletins, AIP supplements
l4_steps.output: Alternate availability confirmed, or replacement alternate identified and approved
l4_steps.kpi: 100% alternate validation completed ≥2 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM closure of a primary alternate (e.g., runway works at Honolulu's divert field) forces complete replanning; NOTAM parsing tools remain largely manual, and auto-filtering tools miss complex conditional NOTAMs issued by some Pacific island states

l4_steps.name: Calculate Equal Time Point and Point of No Return
l4_steps.input: Approved route, winds aloft model, alternate coordinates, single-engine cruise speed profile
l4_steps.output: ETP and PNR coordinates, fuel checkpoint waypoints, go/no-go decision gates embedded in OFP
l4_steps.kpi: ETP calculation within ±2 nm of independent manual cross-check; PNR fuel state verified against aircraft performance tables
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE wind model integration updates every 6 hours; stale wind data on long trans-oceanic sectors (>14 hr block) can shift ETP by up to 40 nm, materially affecting alternate fuel requirements and crew decision windows

l4_steps.name: Review ETOPS significant systems maintenance status
l4_steps.input: Aircraft tech log, ETOPS significant systems check sheet, MEL Part B (ETOPS items)
l4_steps.output: ETOPS airworthiness assessment: all significant systems serviceable or MEL-permissible deferred
l4_steps.kpi: ETOPS maintenance check completed ≥90 min before scheduled departure; zero open ETOPS-critical MEL items at release
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS MEL (Minimum Equipment List) items differ substantively from standard MEL — APU, dual hydraulics, FADEC, SATCOM, and fire suppression must all be assessed against ETOPS-specific criteria; staff confusion on MMEL Part B boundaries generates repeated compliance queries and delays

l4_steps.name: Obtain dual maintenance and operations ETOPS release
l4_steps.input: Completed tech log, ETOPS significant systems sign-off sheet, dispatcher release
l4_steps.output: Dual-signed ETOPS flight release stamped in aircraft tech log and ops system
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ETOPS flights have both maintenance certification and dispatcher release before pushback
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper tech log workflows at outstations create risk of missing or illegible ETOPS-specific entries; digital tech log adoption is incomplete, and remote stations lack AMOS real-time connectivity, causing release delays of 20–45 min

l4_steps.name: Calculate ETOPS fuel requirements
l4_steps.input: ETP coordinates, alternate distances, holding requirements, single-engine fuel burn curves, ETOPS contingency rule (FAR 121 Appendix P / ICAO Annex 6)
l4_steps.output: ETOPS fuel plan: trip fuel + ETOPS reserve + contingency fuel + alternate fuel + final reserve
l4_steps.kpi: ETOPS fuel uplift within ±2% of planned quantity; zero short-fuel departures
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS fuel requirements stack on top of standard dispatch reserves; on maximum-range sectors the cumulative fuel obligation can impose a 3–5 tonne payload penalty, directly reducing revenue yield on high-demand routes

l4_steps.name: Validate ETOPS fuel load against MTOW constraints
l4_steps.system: NAVBLUE Flight Planning / Amadeus Altéa DCS
l4_steps.input: ETOPS fuel plan, passenger count, cargo manifest, zero-fuel weight
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel load with weight-and-balance confirmation; payload trim decision if required
l4_steps.kpi: Zero overweight departures; fuel optimised within 500 kg of minimum legal ETOPS load
l4_steps.pain_point: On peak summer rotations, ETOPS fuel combined with full passenger payload frequently pushes narrow-body aircraft to MTOW; payload trimming displaces revenue passengers and triggers downstream compensation and rebooking costs

l4_steps.name: File ETOPS-annotated ATC flight plan via AFTN
l4_steps.input: Approved ETOPS fuel plan, route with ETP waypoints, alternate airports
l4_steps.output: ATC flight plan filed with ETOPS notation in ICAO Item 18 TBE field; ACK confirmation received
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan filed and acknowledged ≥60 min before scheduled departure; zero unacknowledged plans at departure
l4_steps.pain_point: ICAO Item 18 TBE (ETOPS) field is not consistently parsed by all regional ATC automation systems; Pacific RVSM and North Atlantic Track coordination require secondary manual validation with Shanwick / Oakland Oceanic, adding 15–30 min to filing cycle

l4_steps.name: Monitor ETOPS significant systems via ACARS / SATCOM
l4_steps.input: In-flight ACARS position reports, engine health data (EHM), crew SATCOM check-ins
l4_steps.output: Real-time ETOPS systems status log; alert flags raised for any significant system degradation
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS position report receipt ≤15 min intervals on oceanic tracks; 100% engine health message coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: HF radio dependency in ACARS dead zones (South Pacific, polar routes beyond SATCOM footprint) creates monitoring gaps of 30–60 min; aircraft without Swift Broadband (SBB) upgrade rely on VHF-only ACARS, which drops out on oceanic tracks

l4_steps.name: Update ETOPS alternate weather at ETP crossings
l4_steps.input: Inflight position reports, ETP waypoint schedule, updated TAF / SIGMET bulletins
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go weather assessment for each alternate at projected ETP crossing time
l4_steps.kpi: Weather reassessment delivered to flight crew ≤30 min before each ETP; 100% ETP coverage on all ETOPS sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapidly developing convective weather at oceanic alternates (e.g., Bermuda in Atlantic hurricane season, Midway Atoll in typhoon season) can invalidate ETOPS release post-departure; regulatory requirement to notify crew and assess divert feasibility creates a compressed decision window once the PNR is passed

l4_steps.name: Assess engine or system anomaly for divert decision
l4_steps.input: Engine health alerts, ECAM / EICAS messages reported via SATCOM, crew deviation report
l4_steps.output: Divert decision (continue to destination or proceed to ETOPS alternate); amended routing filed with ATC
l4_steps.kpi: Divert decision communicated within ≤15 min of anomaly detection; ATC re-clearance obtained within ≤20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual authority model (dispatcher + PIC) under FAR 121 for ETOPS divert decisions creates communication latency; SATCOM voice quality on older long-haul narrow-body fleets is often insufficient for complex technical discussions, forcing dispatcher to rely on ACARS text exchange with limited bandwidth

l4_steps.name: Complete ETOPS post-flight operational report
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware / Airline OpsControl
l4_steps.input: Flight data recorder summary, ACARS message logs, crew debrief notes, maintenance findings
l4_steps.output: ETOPS post-flight report compliant with FAR 121.374 / ICAO Doc 10085 Appendix; filed in ops system
l4_steps.kpi: Report filed within 24 hours of landing; 100% compliance rate on regulatory audit cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual aggregation of ACARS logs, crew debrief, and maintenance notes creates a 4–6 hour compilation burden per ETOPS flight; no automated data ingestion pipeline exists in most legacy ops platforms, making timely filing dependent on individual dispatcher diligence

l4_steps.name: Update ETOPS reliability programme and IFSD database
l4_steps.system: AMOS / Aviation Safety Action Programme (ASAP) Portal
l4_steps.input: ETOPS post-flight report, in-flight significant system events, maintenance findings, IFSD occurrences
l4_steps.output: Updated ETOPS reliability metrics report; IFSD rate trend; corrective action initiated if threshold exceeded
l4_steps.kpi: In-Flight Shutdown (IFSD) rate ≤0.02 per 1,000 engine hours (ETOPS-180 regulatory threshold); reliability report issued within 30 days of each reporting period
l4_steps.pain_point: IFSD rate trending requires cross-fleet data aggregation over a 12-month minimum window; smaller operators and new ETOPS entrants fall below the statistical significance threshold required by authorities for self-approval, creating dependency on OEM data sharing and authority-imposed restrictions
